title: Build and linking errors with `use_volk=no` on Linux
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible on `master` (f7fcb79c4399070be07caadfbe2304a9c94711fa)
- Neither error is reproducible on `4.6` (20b44c9575f3d638d1861813003768155fb0fe9a)

### System information

Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX) - AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 threads) - 60.60 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When building current `master` on Linux with `use_volk=no` (to use `vulkan.h`/libvulkan directly), I run into two regressions not present in `4.6`:

1. Linux build fails due to some spurious definitions of `CursorShape` by `Xlib.h` (even showing up in Wayland code) because `vulkan.h` includes it. I might have introduced this one with some includes refactor I did in early 4.7 dev.
2. Linking fails due to ray tracing extension functions not being accessible as global symbols when using libvulkan directly. Introduced in #99119.

```
mold: error: undefined symbol: vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR
>>> referenced by rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp

>>> referenced by rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp

>>> referenced by rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp

collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

I only tested on Linux but issue (2) is probably reproducible on other desktop platforms too.

### Steps to reproduce

`scons p=linuxbsd use_volk=no`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

n/a
